ai.definition: AI-driven robotics is a technology that integrates artificial intelligence into robotic systems to enhance their autonomy, adaptability, and efficiency in performing tasks.
ai.howItWorks: These robots leverage machine learning algorithms to analyze data from sensors and other sources, enabling them to make decisions and adjust their actions based on real-time feedback. This allows for more flexible and precise automation compared to traditional robotics.
ai.problemSolved: AI-driven robotics addresses the limitations of rigid programming in robotic systems by providing a means to handle complex, dynamic environments with varying conditions and tasks.
ai.manufacturing: In manufacturing, AI-driven robots can be used for assembly line operations, quality inspection, material handling, and more, improving productivity and reducing errors.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves selecting appropriate hardware components (e.g., sensors, actuators), integrating AI algorithms, and testing the system in real-world scenarios to ensure reliability and performance.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the complexity of AI algorithms, high-quality sensor integration, robust software development, and ongoing maintenance and updates.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook for AI-driven robotics is positive as more industries recognize its benefits in terms of efficiency and adaptability. However, challenges remain in standardization and regulatory compliance.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by region but generally focus on safety standards, data privacy, and ethical considerations. There are ongoing efforts to establish international guidelines for the use of AI-driven robots.
ai.risks: Risks include potential job displacement, cybersecurity threats, and issues related to bias in decision-making algorithms.
ai.profitability: Profitability can be high due to increased efficiency and reduced labor costs but is also influenced by factors such as initial investment and ongoing maintenance.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may focus on improving AI capabilities, expanding applications across various industries, and addressing regulatory challenges.

glossary.def: A branch of computer science that aims to create systems capable of performing tasks requiring human-like intelligence, such as learning, problem-solving, and decision-making.
A subset of AI that involves algorithms that can learn from and make predictions on data without being explicitly programmed.

subsystems.name: Perception
subsystems.role: senses the workspace and identifies objects, poses and people.
parts: object detection and 6D pose estimation algorithms

subsystems.name: Planning and control
subsystems.role: turns goals into safe, precise motion.

subsystems.name: Manipulation
parts: robotic arms with 6–7 degrees of freedom

subsystems.name: Compute and middleware
subsystems.role: runs AI models in real time on the robot.

subsystems.name: Safety and human interaction
parts: speed and force limiting (e.g. below 140 N contact force)

buildSteps.title: Analyse the task
buildSteps.detail: Define the exact manipulation or navigation job, its variability, cycle time and required accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Collect data
buildSteps.detail: Record human teleoperation demonstrations and generate synthetic scenes in simulation, covering many object poses and lighting conditions.

buildSteps.title: Train models
buildSteps.detail: Use GPUs to train neural networks for perception, grasping and control policies, often starting from a pretrained vision backbone.

buildSteps.title: Validate in simulation
buildSteps.detail: Test policies in a physics simulator with randomised friction, mass and sensor noise to expose weaknesses before touching hardware.

buildSteps.title: Transfer to the real robot
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune with a small amount of real-world data and adjust for the sim-to-real gap, especially for contact-rich tasks.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the stack
buildSteps.detail: Connect perception, planning, control and safety systems on the robot's onboard compute, ensuring real-time performance.

buildSteps.title: Certify safety
buildSteps.detail: Verify force limits, stopping distances and human detection against collaborative robot standards before deployment.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Run in production, log failures and edge cases, and retrain models periodically to improve reliability.

buildSteps.title: Share fleet learning
buildSteps.detail: Aggregate data across many robots so that improvements on one machine benefit the whole fleet.

pathway.milestone: AI in structured tasks such as bin picking, welding and inspection
pathway.unlocks: higher throughput and less reprogramming in factories and warehouses.

pathway.milestone: manipulation skills learned from large demonstration datasets
pathway.unlocks: robots that can handle new objects with minimal retraining.

pathway.milestone: mobile manipulators operating in unstructured spaces like hospitals and farms
pathway.unlocks: automation outside fixed cells, moving between tasks.

pathway.milestone: autonomous humanoid robots with fleet-wide learning
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose assistance for many manual tasks, if safety and reliability are proven.
